text:
Simon Nemec, the second overall pick in 2022, is playing 21.1 minutes a night in Calgary after 155 games in New Jersey. He brings a five-game point streak (2 goals, 3 assists) into the holiday, and his 1.31 points per 60 is above the league rate for defensemen.

The 5v5 numbers are the thing to fix. Calgary gets 51.6% of the shot attempts with him on but only 45.1% of the expected goals, nearly four points worse than without him. The quantity is there; the quality against him isn't.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives reasons for patience. Last season he stopped 18% of the entries aimed at him (a typical defenseman stops 11%) and carried the puck in on 48% of his offensive entries. Evolving-Hockey had him 72nd among 215 defensemen. The Calgary Herald asked this week what his ceiling is, and his goal against Minnesota came on the rush, the part of his game that looks most like a top pick. Only 5% of his shots have gone in; that should rise.
headline: Nemec is finding his game in Calgary
